name: phase3_sparsity
description: Is the sparsity (fraction of zero elements) of a streamed operand buffer
recoverable from package power? This is proposal goal (2) and the Phase 3
core, and it reproduces the lost Figure 2 -- the Eigen/TensorFlow sparsity
code was never committed (confirmed absent from git history).
Victim is ws_sparse_l3_x8: the ws_l3_x8 load stream (8 x 32-byte loads per
iteration from a 4 MB working set), but the buffer is filled to a chosen
density instead of one repeated word. The selector's low 16 bits are the
number of nonzero 32-bit words per 1024 (0..1024); the rest are zero, spread
uniformly by a Bresenham accumulator. The nonzero pattern is 0xFFFFFFFF
(selector high bits 0 -> default all-ones), chosen for maximum SNR on this
first pass; a follow-up can set a realistic int8-packed activation pattern
through the selector's high 32 bits with no code change.
Why this passes work_balance by construction: the byte rate, the addresses
streamed and the loads issued are identical for every density -- only the
*content* of the words (how many are zero) changes. So a contrast between
two densities is a pure operand-content contrast, exactly as the
Hamming-weight sweep was one level down. Config-A, interleaved blocks, one
A/A gate, one anchor.
Condition 0 is density 0 (an all-zero buffer) in every run and condition 1
is the test density, so each run reads as 'power at density d relative to an
all-zero stream'. The polarity control (phase1_polarity) already showed the
condition index carries no bias, so no reverse arm is needed; the A/A is
carried as the per-session gate.
Densities are concentrated at the low-density (high-sparsity) end, which is
the ML-relevant regime: post-ReLU activations are 50-90% zero, i.e. density
brackets the rest for the full curve. Density 1024 (all nonzero, all-ones)
is bit-identical to ws_l3_x8 holding 0xFFFFFFFF and anchors this session to
the Phase 1 sweeps (expect ~+1.9 W, cf. hw32 and l3_forward).
Expected shape: monotone rise with density, steepest at the 0->nonzero
boundary (Phase 1's +349 mW cheap-zero step), so the very sparse levels
should already separate from baseline -- which is what makes sparsity
recoverable. Read with analysis.report per run for the gates, then the
sparsity classifier/regressor over the whole set (see summary.cmd).
warmup_blocks 4: ws_sparse_l3_x8 populates 2 x 4 MB per thread, as ws_l3_x8
does; four blocks removes the fault-in transient at ~0.5 s cost per run.
